title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E420 Euler re-founds the calculus of variations without Lagrange's special δ-symbol. He embeds the given curve y = X(x) in a one-parameter family y = y(x,t) with y(x,0) = X. The variation of any expression is then its partial increment in t at fixed x, written dt·(dZ/dt). This page completes §7 and gives §8.

§7 (end): With p = y_x, q = y_xx, r = y_xxx, the rules for differentiating functions of two variables give
- ∂p/∂t = ∂²y/∂x∂t,
- ∂q/∂t = ∂³y/∂x²∂t,
- ∂r/∂t = ∂⁴y/∂x³∂t.
These rest on the interchangeability of mixed partial derivatives. Euler adds a reading rule for the notation (d³y/dx²dt): differentiate y three times, twice with only x varying and once with only t varying, dropping the simple differentials dx, dt after each step.

§8: Let Z = Z(x, y, p, q, r, …) with ordinary differential dZ = M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + …. For the variation one sets
- dx = 0,
- dy = dt·y_t,
- dp = dt·y_xt,
- dq = dt·y_xxt,
- dr = dt·y_xxxt.
Hence ∂Z/∂t = N y_t + P y_xt + Q y_xxt + R y_xxxt + …. In modern terms this is the first variation δZ = Z_y δy + Z_p (δy)' + Z_q (δy)'' + …, with δy = y_t dt; that is, the Gateaux derivative of Z along the family. It also uses the commutation δ(d^k y/dx^k) = d^k(δy)/dx^k.

§9 begins the third kind of expression, the integral functional ∫Z dx. The next page differentiates under the integral sign and later integrates by parts to reach the Euler–Lagrange expression.
errors: No mathematical errors. The interchange of mixed partials is assumed without comment, which is standard for Euler. Minor notational inconsistency in the original: (d³y/dx².dt) is printed with a dot in the explanatory sentence but without one elsewhere.

ideas.what: Variation defined as the partial derivative with respect to an auxiliary parameter t of a one-parameter family of curves y(x,t) through the given curve
ideas.modern_name: First variation as Gateaux/directional derivative along a one-parameter family of admissible functions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E420 (1771/72), as his reinterpretation of Lagrange's δ-method; standard in Goldstine's and Fraser's histories
ideas.where_published: E420 itself (Novi Commentarii 16, 1772); companion papers E385 and E386 on the calculus of variations

ideas.what: Commutation of variation and x-differentiation via equality of mixed partials: ∂(∂^k y/∂x^k)/∂t = ∂^{k+1}y/∂x^k∂t
ideas.modern_name: δ and d commute; Schwarz/Clairaut symmetry of mixed partials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E44, c. 1734–40) and Clairaut for mixed partials; Lagrange for δd = dδ
ideas.where_published: E44 'De infinitis curvis eiusdem generis'; Institutiones calculi integralis vol. III appendix

ideas.what: Chain rule giving the first variation of the integrand Z(x,y,p,q,r,…)
ideas.modern_name: First variation of a Lagrangian density: δZ = Σ ∂Z/∂y^{(k)} · (δy)^{(k)}
ideas.where_published: E420; Institutiones calculi integralis III (Appendix de calculo variationum)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the well-documented core of Euler's parameter-based reformulation of the variational calculus in E420. The parameter method, the commuting partials and the chain rule are all standard and credited to Euler and Lagrange in the histories. Nothing on the page is new or overlooked.
transcription_corrections: Long-s renderings ('meminiffe', 'fi', 'fola', 'fumatur', 'fimplicia', 'feu', 'fcribi', 'fequitur', 'quaefita', 'diuifione', 'expreffio', 'propofita', 'fit') should read meminisse, si, sola, sumatur, simplicia, seu, scribi, sequitur, quaesita, diuisione, expressio, proposita, sit.
Previous page: the section number 7 is printed twice (the source has §7 twice, so the second should logically be §7a or the numbering is off by one). This page's §8 follows the source.
